MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]

Specimen Type: Whole blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Suspected Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers to amplify short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. DNA was extracted from whole blood using standard protocols. Multiple informative STR markers were analyzed for each chromosome to assess copy number. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine the presence or absence of trisomy.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed

Result: rsa(13,18,21)×2

INTERPRETATION
PCR analysis is consistent with a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this sample.

LIMITATIONS
• This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only
• Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be reliably detected
• Segmental imbalances, balanced rearrangements, and other structural abnormalities are not detected by this method
• This test does not exclude other chromosomal or genetic abnormalities

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is indicated based on these results. If clinical suspicion for a chromosomal imbalance remains, please contact the laboratory to discuss additional testing options.
